`recall --evidence` returns `<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>` text as `role: "user"` evidence when it is the content of a user turn. This happens with native claude-code records, both when `message.content` is a plain string and when it is a text block:

```json

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>"}]}}
```

`docs/recall-evidence.md` (lines 42-43) says: "Structured hidden reasoning, tool output, system instructions and metadata are not returned as conversation text." That holds for system-role records, which the evidence path drops. It doesn't hold for reminder text inside a user turn.

The other conversation readers already skip these turns. In the run below, `conversationSubstantiveRequest` returns "" for both reminder lines, while the evidence path returns them as user spans. In that run the two reminder spans also came out ahead of the real user request.

### Repro

`main` @ f8deab17, Go 1.27.3, linux/amd64, run in a clean `env -i` with a throwaway HOME/GOPATH/GOCACHE. This is a throwaway test in `internal/cli` (not committed). {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>zebrafoo block-form reminder</system-reminder>"}]}}
```
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"please fix the zebrafoo parser"}]}}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Fixed the zebrafoo parser."}]}}
{"type":"system","content":"zebrafoo system-role record"}
```

Output:

```
state=available warnings=[] spans=4
EVIDENCE line=1 pointer=/message/content role="user" text="<system-reminder>zebrafoo string-form reminder</system-reminder>"
EVIDENCE line=2 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="user" text="<system-reminder>zebrafoo block-form reminder</system-reminder>"
EVIDENCE line=4 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="assistant" text="Fixed the zebrafoo parser."

CONVERSATION line=1 conversationSubstantiveRequest=""
CONVERSATION line=2 conversationSubstantiveRequest=""
CONVERSATION line=3 conversationSubstantiveRequest="please fix the zebrafoo parser"
```

The system-role record on line 5 is dropped as expected. Lines 1 and 2 are returned as user evidence.

Compact v1 transcripts don't produce evidence on `main` at all yet. #564 adds that, and with #564 compact `<system-reminder>` user turns behave the same way. I didn't change that in #564 because this gap predates compact support.

Wrapper or system-reminder text inside a user turn isn't returned as user conversation evidence, the same way system-role records aren't.

The evidence path uses neither.

### Possible direction (your call)

One option is to skip user-role fields in `evidenceJSONFields` when the text matches the same wrapper predicate the other readers use. Another is a narrower check just for `<system-reminder>`-style wrappers. Note that `isWrapperRequest` drops any user text that starts with `<`, which may be broader than you want for evidence. The third option is to keep the behavior and change the docs to say that reminder text inside a user turn can show up. Which one fits the evidence contract is up to you.

Related to #412 and #534, and a companion to #560. **This PR is based on `main` and doesn't depend on #560.** It builds, passes and can merge either before or after #560 (details under "Relation to #560"). Not marked as fixing either issue, for the same reason as #560: #557 fixed the main symptom, and I don't know whether you consider those issues done.

The commits don't carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. I don't have a supported agent session to capture them from, and I didn't want to fake any.

## Why

Compact v1 records (`{"v":1,"type":"user"|"assistant","content":[...]}`, what the default export writes for claude-code, codex and pi) put the content at the record's top level, with no `message` wrapper. #557 taught the conversation, history-fragment and eval-gen readers to read that. Three more readers still look only inside `message`, and each one is broken on `main` (failing output below):

- **`episode_tools.go`**: `toolCallsFromObj` reads assistant content only from `message.content`. In a compact session it finds no `tool_use` blocks, so every episode has empty `ToolSequence` / `CommandSequence`. Episode segmentation on `main` already recognizes compact user turns, so the episodes exist but have no tools in them.
- **`pattern_corpus_enrich.go`**: `corpusEpisodeOps` has the same problem, so compact sessions add no `episode_tools`, `episode_commands` or file refs to the pattern corpus.
- **`recall_evidence_source.go`**: `evidenceJSONFields` produces no fields for compact records. Every compact session is marked `partial` with "contains unreadable or unsupported conversation content" and never returns an evidence span. Compact user text blocks also have no `type` (`{"text":"..."}`), and compact records keep the turn time in `ts`, not `timestamp`.

## What changed

- `episode_tools.go`, `pattern_corpus_enrich.go`: when a record has no `message` wrapper, read the assistant content from the top level. This is the same fallback `history.go` and `conversation.go` already use on `main`.
- `recall_evidence_source.go`: if a `user`/`assistant`/`message` record has no `message` key, its content is read from the top level with JSON pointers under `/content`, untyped `{"text":...}` blocks are accepted, and `ts` is used when `timestamp` is absent. All three only apply to records without a `message` key, so native claude-code, codex and opencode parsing is unchanged. Tool output (`tool_use.result`), images and thinking blocks are still excluded.
- `patterns.IndexerVersion` 9 → 10. The corpus skips a session when its size, mtime, sha and parser version are unchanged. A compact transcript's bytes don't change on upgrade, so without the bump, sessions already indexed with empty tool ops would stay that way. Earlier reader changes bumped this version the same way (see `docs/pattern_v2.md`).
- Episode projection versioned too. The bump above only reaches the SQLite corpus. `refreshPatternLayer` skips rebuilding `patterns/episodes.ndjson` (and the tasks, procedures and practices built from it) while the sessions fingerprint is unchanged, and an upgrade doesn't change it. The patterns source in the manifest now records `extraction_version` (the `patterns.IndexerVersion` that built the episodes), and `patternSourceCurrent` treats a different version as stale. Sources written before the field read as 0 and rebuild once. `patterns status` uses the same check, so it reports them `stale` until then.

Two commits: the reader fix with the version bump, then the episode-projection version and compact `ts`.

**Rebased onto current `main` (6c4b11de).** The only conflict was in `episodes.go`. #589 removed `PrivacyIdentity` from the pattern source. So `patternSourceCurrent` now compares only the sessions fingerprint and `ExtractionVersion`, and the `ExtractionVersion` it writes is just `patterns.IndexerVersion`. The commit message was updated to match.

## Relation to #560

#560 adds a `transcriptRecordContent` helper and compact fixtures in `history_compact_transcript_test.go`. This PR uses neither, so it doesn't depend on #560:

- The two tool-op readers use `main`'s existing inline fallback instead of the helper. If #560 merges, they can switch to `transcriptRecordContent` in a one-line follow-up.
- The fixtures live in `compact_transcript_ops_fixtures_test.go`, under different names (`compactOps{Claude,Codex,Pi}Transcript`), so the two PRs don't declare the same symbols. Their content is the same as #560's fixtures. Once both are in, one set can be deleted.
- Both PRs add an `ExtractionVersion` field to `internal/manifest`, but on different structs (`PatternSource` here, `HistorySource` in #560).

Checked against #560 rebased onto the same `main` (b7b4fb55): merging it with this branch is clean (git merge, no conflicts), and on the merged tree `go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1` passes. So it doesn't matter which one merges first.

## Tests

- `TestEpisodeToolSequencesCompactTranscript`, `TestBuildBrainEpisodesCompactTranscriptToolSequences` (the second goes through `buildBrainEpisodes`)
- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactTranscript`, `TestPatternCorpusReindexesCompactTranscriptToolOps`. The second builds the corpus, then models a v9 corpus (parser_version 9, tool ops deleted) and rebuilds.
- `TestRecallEvidenceCompactTranscript`: checks the exact fields per line, role and pointer. It also checks that every pointer resolves to the reported string in the source line, that no tool output leaks, and that each field's timestamp is the record's `ts`.
- `TestRefreshPatternLayerRebuildsEpisodesFromOlderExtractor`: builds the episode layer, rewrites it the way the old reader left it (same episodes, no tool ops, no `extraction_version`), then runs a normal (non-forced) `refreshPatternLayer`.
